articleTitle: YOLOv8 Based Deep Learning Method for Potholes Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Potholes are a common road hazard that may cause significant damage to vehicles and pose risks to drivers and pedestrians. The detection and classification of potholes in images can aid in effective maintenance and repair of road infrastructure. In this study, the training of YOLOv8, an advanced object detection algorithm, on a pothole image dataset is presented. The pothole image dataset consists of diverse images captured from various road conditions and environments. The dataset is annotated with bounding boxes around the pothole instances to facilitate supervised learning. YOLOv8, known for its accuracy and efficiency, is utilized as the object detection framework due to its real-time object detection ability. To train YOLOv8, a two-step procedure is followed. Firstly, a pre-training phase is conducted on a large-scale COCO dataset. This pre-trained model is fine-tuned on the pothole image dataset. The fine-tuning process adapts the pre-trained model to accurately detect and classify potholes. The performance of the trained YOLOv8 model is evaluated. This proposed approach is able to accurately detect and classify potholes in images. In this work YOLOv8 is used for pothole detection. Different variants of YOLOv8 (YOLOv8x, YOLOv81, YOLOv8m, YOLOv8s, YOLOv8n) are used and then the results on the dataset “Pothole detection Image Dataset” is analysed. Overall, this study presents a comprehensive framework for training YOLOv8 on a pothole image dataset.

articleTitle: Weed Detection Using AlexN et in Sesame Crops
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Farming is the most essential part of humans for food. Rapid population growth increases the demand for more prominent functional capacity in agriculture. Yet, some issues, such as weeds, pose challenges to harvesting good crop yield, like absorbing nutrients, water, and light to minimize gain productively. To increase crop yield, humans spray weed-destructive toxins over the crop to destroy weeds. However, this also dilapidates crops and brings uncertainty to human food production. Recently, computer vision-based methods have been applied to automatically recognize weeds in the crop field by analyzing filed images for properties such as color, size, shape, shading, and texture. This paper utilizes an AlexN et-8 architecture to detect weeds in a field of Sesame crops. AlexN et architecture consists of8layers in a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The experimental analysis on 1300 Sesame crop images showed that the presented AlexN et architecture-based model achieved 97.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy on RGB images.

articleTitle: Accounting for Groundtruth Subjectivity in Comparing Face Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Security is the key concern of the family during the commute of the family members from home to work and vice-a-versa. Ensuring safety of the passengers is the responsibility of the administration. All these systems comprise of surveillance camera and inspection apparatus to initiate driven action for circumvention of mishap. Deploying a secure system is a crucial part of driver monitoring system and advanced driver assistance system for entire range of multi-carrier vehicles. A collateral and efficient safety system can be accomplished with the artificial intelligence based face recognition techniques. Face detection is the dominant step for successful face recognition. Selection of deserving face detection method is restricted by the scale, profile, styling accessories, radiance, barrier etc. Localizing the face in video or an image briskly with desired accuracy is often challenging. Comparative analysis for various state of art artificial intelligence based face detection models is fulfilled amidst of uniform performance metrics such as inference time and mean average precision. Leveraging the balance between detection time and accuracy can empower the administration of the system on an embedded platform. It also essential to have knowledge about the model size, benefits and limitation offered by each model.

articleTitle: V2V and V2I Communication Using CAM Protocol in V2X Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant surge in the manufacturing of autonomous driving cars. Various car manufacturers are engaged in fierce competition to bring the best autonomous vehicles to the market. Companies like “Tesla” have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of autonomous driving, greatly impacting the automotive industry. Two key technologies that have played a pivotal role in autonomous driving are “ADAS” and “CV2X”. DENM (Decentralized Environmental Notification Message) is a message format utilized in Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems (C-ITS) to facilitate the exchange of information about environmental hazards or situations among vehicles and infrastructure. The CAM (Cooperative Awareness Message) messaging format is an integral part of cooperative intelligent transportation systems (C-ITS) that facilitates the real-time exchange of information between vehicles and infrastructure units. It allows vehicles to share their status, position, and basic information with nearby entities, enabling cooperative and coordinated actions. The main objective of CAM is to provide situational awareness to nearby vehicles and infrastructure units in real-time. Upon closer examination, it becomes evident that the CAM and DENM messaging formats share similarities, but their functionalities are distinct. Both messaging formats are highly efficient and offer significant benefits. We have implemented V2V and V2I communication using CAM message format to ensure connectivity and message exchange between V2V and V2I.

articleTitle: Open Set Masked Face Identification system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: From healthcare workers to working professionals, wearing a facial mask became a new normal owing to the COVID-19 pandemic, and hence, the need for reliable and efficient open set masked face identification systems has never been more critical. In this research, we successfully developed and implemented a robust model capable of identifying individuals and accurately detecting imposters even when facial coverings are present. To achieve this, we endeavored to create a custom dataset by combining two publicly available datasets and experimented with various state-of-the-art models through transfer learning to get the best solution. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, showcasing the potential of open set masked face identification systems in addressing security challenges in diverse domains, from healthcare facilities to corporate environments. We saw a 65% accuracy in closed set identification along with a False Accept Rate (FAR) of 0.096 and False Reject Rate (FRR) 0.102 of at a threshold of 0.94 for open set identification. Our findings aspire to contribute to a safer and more secure future as we navigate the new normal of mask-wearing in a post COVID-19 world.

articleTitle: Unlinkability of Biometric Templates Using Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Biometric authentication is widely used but raises privacy and security concerns due to the vulnerability of biometric templates stored in centralized databases. To protect biometric templates, the ISO/IEC 24745 standard established two requirements: irreversibility and unlinkability. While most existing approaches compromise unlinkability, we propose a novel approach to achieving both requirements using HD wallets to change the password hash stored in the database periodically. This approach ensures that compromised biometric templates cannot be used for future authentication, protecting user privacy and security. Our approach offers a high level of security and privacy while maintaining usability for users. By periodically changing the password hash, we ensure that even if an attacker gains access to a user's biometric template, it cannot be used for future authentication, reducing the risk of unauthorized access to sensitive information.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotion Classification Through Speech and Correlated Emotional Sounds via a Variational Auto-Encoder Model with Prosodic Regularization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Recent studies have explored the development of empathetic systems, capable of engaging in human-like communication and support in daily life tasks. This envision primarily requires the correct classification of human emotions in speech. Nevertheless, it is challenged by the complexities of classifying emotionally similar or overlapped audio content characteristics, such as between “Neutral” and “Sad” emotions, or “Angry” and “Happy” emotions, representing more than 17.42 percent of misclassifications. Furthermore, existing emotional databases, while publicly available, often contain weakly emotional data, posing challenges for both human listeners and artificial classification systems. In this paper, we proposed an emotionally regularised variational auto-encoder model for the classification of emotional speech audios with correlated emotional sounds, particularly for emotions with overlapping audio attributes. The dataset proposed is a mixed dataset, created from a public well-known dataset, and extended with real added customised data. The customised data are distinctive emotional sounds, such as shouting, crying, giggling, etc. Our emotion classifier model can classify four emotions, such as “Angry”, “Sad”, “Happy” and “Normal”. The sounds selected are associated with the selected emotions and the speaker gender. Throughout the training of the variational auto-encoder model and the classifier, we aligned our complex data with prosodic features, to obtain a more emotionally expected quality. The results show that the emotional sounds in speech and the speech utterances, are strongly complementary for a real emotional speech classification with a test accuracy of 0.973, improving the vanilla VAE with 0.881, and the standard CNN-based model with 0.652.

articleTitle: Code-Mixing and Code-Switching on Social Media Text: A Brief Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In the diverse linguistic landscape of India, individuals employ a variety of languages (codes) in their online communications, much like non-English speakers worldwide. Code-mixing is predominating in today's communication-driven culture and no natural language has escaped these trends. This paper explores the expanding subfield of Natural Language Processing (NLP) known as code mixing (CM) and code switching (CS). It examines how individuals exhibit their linguistic versatility by seamlessly blending English terms with regional languages (e.g., English-Hindi, English-Punjabi, English-Telugu) through techniques such as transliteration, Romanization, and language fusion on popular social media platforms such as Facebook, Google Reviews, and Twitter. The pervasive use of social media applications has resulted in a substantial influx of unstructured text, much of which is characterized by code-mixing and multi-script writing, where words are expressed in scripts distinct from their native tongue.

articleTitle: An Emerging Fire Detection System based on Convolutional Neural Network and Aerial-Based Forest Fire Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Accidents caused by undiscovered fires have resulted in substantial financial losses around the world, emphasizing the critical need for robust fire detection systems. Existing fire and smoke detectors have demonstrated inefficiencies, forcing the development of more sophisticated alternatives. Based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) technology, this research provides a novel fire detection system. By researching fire flame features and utilising edge detection and thresholding algorithms, the system accomplishes real-time fire detection by analyzing live camera data. A fire detection model is developed that can detect dangerous fires based on their size, velocity, volume, and texture. The experimental findings of our model on a fire dataset that we created ourselves show its strong fire detection capability, especially in real-time multi-scale fire detection. We use the YOLOv4 protocol, the Darknet deep learning framework, and a new network topology to build the fire detection model. A large-scale, multi-scale system is used for extensive training and testing, outperforming previous methods in terms of the accuracy of fire detection.

articleTitle: Hybrid Convolutional Neural Networks To Create An Attack Detection Framework For A Wireless Sensor Network Based Health Care Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Healthcare Wireless Sensor Networks (H-WSNs) play a crucial role in modern healthcare applications, enabling remote patient monitoring and data collection. A unique Hybrid Deep Learning Model (HDML) for attack detection in H-WSNs is presented in this paper. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks are combined to create HDML, which enables the efficient detection of common, black, and grey hole attacks. The proposed approach comprises three phases: pre-processing, dimensionality reduction, and attack detection. For the purpose of facilitating subsequent analysis, patient health data is pre-processed using the one-hot encoding technique. We use the Modified Huber Independent Component Analysis based Squirrel Search Algorithm (MHICA-SSA) for dimensionality reduction to successfully reduce data size without compromising important information, overcoming the shortcomings of H-WSNs. The heart of the attack detection system is the CNN-LSTM model, which leverages the spatial feature extraction capabilities of CNNs and the temporal dependencies captured by LSTM networks. This powerful combination allows for accurate and efficient identification of malicious activities within the H-WSN. In order to verify the efficacy of HDML, we implement the suggested framework in the NS2 network simulator and assess its performance using a variety of performance metrics, such as packet delivery ratio, false alarm rate, network lifespan, energy consumption, throughput, and attack detection time and rate. This research contributes to enhancing the security and performance of H-WSNs, making them more robust and reliable for healthcare applications. In comparison to current methods, the suggested methodology increases throughput by up to 3.3 times and network lifetime by up to 4 times.

articleTitle: Detection Analysis of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Modified DensNet-121
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Diabetes is a prevalent illness that affects the health of many people in today's society. With a significant increase in the number of diabetic patients in India, there has been a rise in associated diseases that are affecting the community. Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is an example of a silent disease that can occur as a result of either Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes and can lead to permanent blindness if not diagnosed promptly. However, the manual screening of DR by ophthalmologists is a time-consuming process. Therefore, this paper aims to use Deep Learning (DL) to analyze various DR stages and develop a unique methodology for detecting diabetic retinopathy. By utilizing a modified pre-trained DenseNet-121 architecture and improved pre-processing techniques, our model is able to detect diabetic retinopathy with greater accuracy. The model was trained on a large dataset to automatically identify the DR stage. The DR stages are classified into five categories, ranging from 0 to 4. The input parameters for our model were the patient's fundus eye images, as described in this paper. Our model outperformed the discussed state-of-the-art models with an accuracy of 97%.

articleTitle: Unveiling Image Classifiers: An In-Depth ComparativeExploration of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The challenging problem of image classification serves as a critical hub with important implications for a variety of fields in the rapidly growing field of computational intelligence. This research study carries out on an in-depth journey, carefully traversing through a broad range of machine learning algorithms carefully made for the important task of image classification. The main goal of this research is to understand the unique properties, natural obstacles, and elaborate metrics for performance that such algorithms feature. The work develops through a broad and thorough comparative examination, thoroughly analyzing the positive aspects and flaws of each method. The broad Support Vector Machines (SVM), the fundamental Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), the combined skill of Random Forest, the perceptive K- Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and the interpretable Decision Trees make up the set of algorithms that went through comprehensive examination. This extensive research provided an array of findings that are ready to give an illumination on both the individual capability of these algorithms and their combined impact on the broad area of image classification. This research gives a map for analyzing the complex details that support the effectiveness and contributions of these algorithms within the dynamic world of image classification through the integration of real-life data with logical interpretations.

articleTitle: Improving Threat Object Recognition for X-Ray Baggage Screening Using Distraction Removal Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: X-ray security screening plays an important role in maintaining safety and security at railway stations, airports, and in the transportation system. This process involves the inspection and examination of luggage and personal belongings to detect threat items and explosive items. The complexity of luggage and baggage scanning can indeed make threat detection challenging. This paper proposes a method to improve visual search tasks in baggage security screening by utilizing automatic instance segmentation act as a diagnostic aid, drawing the screener's attention towards the threat items. This involves an inpainting method using regionfill to automatically detect and remove benign objects from the image. The average confidence score of the detected item after the regionfill approach is increased from 98% to 99.5% for threat items (gun, knife, shuriken, blade). By integrating an automatic segmentation model and inpainting methods, this work offers a promising avenue for improving the effectiveness of X-ray screening procedures in identifying potential threats.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Fault Detection in DC Motors and the Role of Mounting Configurations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Unexpected motor failures can halt industrial operations and have an impact on productivity, security, and profitability. To overcome these challenges, this work presents an AI-based method for industrial DC motor monitoring. The k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) machine learning model used by this tool to analyze sensor data successfully detects and predicts motor problems, enabling preventative maintenance. This technology improves industrial operations by lowering repair expenses, downtime, and safety. For performance study, we evaluated this algorithm with both vertical and horizontal installation. Vertical mounting performed better than horizontal installation under fully loaded situations. On the test set, the k-NN model accurately identified and predicted motor defects with an accuracy of 95.22 percent. According to this study, our AI-enabled tool can increase industrial safety and productivity.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Video Editing Capabilities of Text-to-Video Generators Using DDPM Inversion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Text-to-video generation has garnered significant attention due to its potential applications in various domains, such as video synthesis, content creation, and entertainment. The one-shot learning approach, wherein a single text-video pair is utilized for generating corresponding videos, has emerged as a promising technique in this realm. This approach involves the generation of videos based on a given text prompt, with subsequent editing to refine the output. However, existing methods often exhibit limitations in achieving intricate and nuanced video editing. In this research paper, we present an innovative framework that enhances the editing capabilities of one-shot text-to-video generation models. We propose the integration of the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) inversion technique into the existing pipeline. Initially, a single text-video pair is used to guide the initial generation process, yielding a foundational video output. To address the challenge of limited editing potential, we leverage DDPM inversion, a novel method capable of iteratively refining and modifying the generated video's structure while preserving high-level content details.

articleTitle: Efficient Approximate Vedic Multiplier: Design, Analysis, and Application in Image Blending
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Approximate computing has become a widely recognized method for designing energy-efficient arithmetic architectures in the context of error-tolerant applications. This paper presents the design and analysis of a 4-bit approximate Vedic multiplier (AVMT) using the Urdhva Tiryagbhyam method. This Vedic approach, involving vertical and crosswise steps, outperforms traditional multiplication in terms of efficiency. An approximate 2-bit multiplier (AVM2) is designed, and an AVMT is proposed using AVM2. The proposed architecture has better propagation delay and less area utilization compared to other conventional multipliers. AVMT has an 11% reduction in area consumption and a 12% increase in processing speed compared to the exact Vedic multiplier. To assess its practicality in real-world scenarios, the proposed multiplier is integrated into an image-blending application. The results indicate that the system achieves a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) average value of 0.91, which proves to be suitable for error-resilient image processing applications.

articleTitle: An Efficient Correlated Gamma Wave-Based Lightweight Model for Schizophrenia Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Schizophrenia is a serious mental disorder that affects a person's ability to think, feel, and behave clearly. Schizophrenia detection using Electroencephalography is an en-grossing area of neuroscience. There are several researches reported on designing effective models which can detect schizophre-nia accurately, however, existing models are either complex or use an extensive number of waves to process for detecting schizophre-nia accurately. Addressing the issues mentioned above, this work presents a lightweight Schizophrenia detection model with the help of Gamma wave extraction from the electroencephalogram brain waves. The proposed model has approximately 12500 parameters with an accuracy of 99.5 % which is much lighter than the previous state-of-the-art models that contain nearly 11 million parameters. We also presented a detailed comparative result analysis among all the state-of-the-art models with the proposed model which shows the effectiveness of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Optimizing Identification Time in Fingerprint Recognition Using Cuckoo Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Fingerprint recognition is a widely used method for biometric identification. However, matching fingerprints in large databases can be a slow and challenging process. This work proposes an indexing-based framework that uses the Cuckoo filter to overcome this issue. The approach involves initially generating a fixed-length feature vector using minutia cylinder code (MCC) from fingerprint images. These feature vectors are then hashed and stored in the Cuckoo filter, enabling efficient retrieval of query fingerprint templates and reducing the search space. The proposed method is evaluated and compared to the existing Bloom filter-based approach using the FVC-2002 fingerprint dataset. The results show that the proposed method achieves higher retrieval accuracy, lower equal error rate (EER) and faster query times compared to the existing Bloom filter-based approach. In the best case, we achieved a Genuine Match Rate (GMR) = 100% at a False match rate (FMR) = 0%, thus indicating a perfect model performance. Hence, our obtained results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method for fingerprint identification.

articleTitle: Enhancing Large Document Organization Through Effective Preprocessing and Data Embedding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper proposes an effective document classification system that utilizes modified data pre-processing and embedding techniques. Here a model is proposed that compares various machine learning techniques, such as SVM, KNN, and NB, using different pre-processing and data embedding methods. The model's accuracy was tested on two datasets - a multiclass news dataset and a binary IMDB dataset - and the results demonstrate that SVM with TF -IDF achieved an accuracy rate of 95 per cent. These results indicate that the proposed approach offers a reliable and efficient method for handling huge quantities of documents while streamlining the classification procedure.

articleTitle: Intelligent Mobile Channel Estimation and Inter Carrier Interference Cancelation for 5G Services in Indian Shinkansen “Bullet Train”
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In recent years, the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Generation mobile communication system (5G) has become increasingly popular and is about to meet the growing demand from mobile and IoT devices such as smartphones and drones. As railroads and other modes of transportation become faster, it has become increasingly important to consider communications in high-speed moving environments. In an extremely high-speed moving environment, the Doppler effect occurs for radio waves, resulting in loss of data received and transmitted by mobile terminal. In this paper, we aimed to prevent performance degradation of 5G communications by using Inter-Carrier Interference Cancelation between OFDM sub-carriers of 5G based on Delay and Doppler Profiler as a new signal processing technology to correct the received signal in a high-speed moving environment targeting high-speed trains and bullet trains in India. Simulations of the communication quality of four modulations, Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK), 16Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM), 64QAM, and 256QAM, were performed in two situations at speeds of 150km/h and 350kmlh. The simulation results show that the Inter-Carrier Interference Canceller used in this study can improve the Bit Error Rate. It was also shown that the error rate of the communication can be further reduce by increasing the number of neighboring sub carriers considered for Doppler shift rejection.

articleTitle: SentiNet: Empowering Robust Loan Default Prediction through Ensemble Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Loan default prediction is a critical task for lending institutions to minimize financial risks. This research paper presents a comprehensive analysis of loan default prediction using the Lending Club dataset. The study includes data filtering, exploratory data analysis (EDA), data standardization, and the application of basic machine learning (ML) models followed by an ensemble model. Initially, the dataset undergoes data filtering and EDA to eliminate irrelevant features and gain insights. Missing values are handled, and potential outliers are detected. EDA techniques reveal variable distributions, correlations, and patterns relevant to loan default prediction. Basic ML models, such as logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests, are trained on the preprocessed data for loan default prediction. These models achieve an accuracy of approximately 73%. To further enhance prediction accuracy, an ensemble learning approach is employed. The ensemble model combines the predictions of multiple individual models, resulting in improved accuracy of 76.8%. Additionally, the model maintains an 80% loan approval rate, striking a balance between risk mitigation and providing credit access. To assess model consistency, k-fold cross-validation is applied. This technique evaluates the model's performance by training and testing on different subsets of the dataset. The results demonstrate the ensemble model's stability and reliability across multiple folds.

articleTitle: 5G High Speed DRONE Air Logistics Supported by Advanced 5G Mobile Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper proposes an inter-carrier interference (ICI) canceling OFDM receiver for 5G mobile systems to support high-speed drone logistics at 200 km/h. Such a highspeed drone receiver sees a transmission path consisting of multiple Doppler-shifted propagation channels. the ICI canceller compensates for the ICI generated when the subcarriers lose orthogonality due to the Doppler spread channel. the DMRS (Demodulation Reference Symbol) pilot signal is used to analyze three parameters: distance attenuation of each multipath amplitude component, relative delay time, and frequency deviation due to Doppler shift. ICI cancellation is achieved by generating a channel transfer function (CTF) based on the three parameters and applying the ICI inverse operation. The performance of the ICI cancellation was simulated for the channel conditions specific to high-speed drones, such as 200 km/h, and 5 path reverse Doppler shift for QPSK and 16QAM modulations. By increasing the number of taps in the Multi-Tap Equalizer, the improvement in BER was significant.

articleTitle: Machine Translation Techniques using AI : A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Automation of natural language translation is undergoing a significant evolution, with various approaches emerging over the years. In the context of a vast and diverse country like India, where numerous regional languages are spoken, and people frequently move for various reasons such as- trade, migration, education, tourism, and more- the need for a robust translation mechanism becomes paramount to overcome language barriers. This article delves into the research efforts of various scholars in the field of machine translation and explores the future prospects in this domain. Additionally, it provides insights into the diverse Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence methodologies employed in Machine Translation.

articleTitle: Blackgram Plant Leaves Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Agriculture is an essential sector that provides direct and indirect to economic growth. New technologies are constantly developing according to the changes and demands from the Agricultural sector. It is more important to conduct routine crop monitoring to identify diseases in their early stages and enhance crop yields. Black gram, a vital pulse crop cultivated across the nation, leads to annual financial losses for farmers as it is vulnerable to various diseases that impact crop yields. The diseases commonly detected and frequently observed are Anthracnose, Powdery Mildew, and Yellow-mosaic. If this crop is affected due to diseases, this will not only affect the agricultural sector but also affect people's health like developing allergies and in most severe cases can also cause food poisoning. Early detection of such diseases will prevent the loss of crop yield. The various diseases require different treatments so it is important to identify the diseases more accurately. We strongly believe that we can significantly contribute to the society in developing a healthy lifestyle and to the agricultural industry in producing quality products.

articleTitle: Intelligent Constellation Generation based on Autoencoder Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper discusses intelligent constellation generation based on autoencoder communication system. In previous studies, the amplitude was set to fluctuate between r=0.0 and 1.0. However, when checking the generated constellation, distortion was confirmed instead of the conventional symbol arrangement. Therefore, in this paper, it compares the case where the amplitude is constant, the case where the average amplitude within a Minibatch is 1, and the case where the average amplitude is 1 for Interval time. The communication standard used in this research is IEEE 802.11a, assuming wireless Local Area Network (LAN) specifications. The IEEE 802.11a standard has an Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) length of 64, a subcarrier number of 52, and Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) and 16 Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM), modulation methods. A guard interval of 800 ns is added and the symbol length is 4000 ns. First, a simulation was performed under the condition that the amplitude was kept constant. QPSK with 4 symbols, constant amplitude model is rounded more than previous research result. 16QAM with 16 symbols is arranged regularly like lined up on a line. Second, the simulation was performed under the condition that the average amplitude within the minibatch was set to 1. QPSK with 4 symbols, appears to rotate clockwise. 16QAM with 16 symbols has a more uniform symbol placement than previous research result. Third, a simulation was performed under the condition that the average amplitude within Interval time was set to 1. QPSK with 4 symbols, is the closest to square among QPSK output results so far. The direction is slightly tilted, but if it can be rotated a little more, it may be possible to reproduce the same symbol arrangement as before. 16QAM with 16 symbols, the symbol arrangement is biased as a whole. However, it can be seen that are arranged in line on the line, perhaps due to regularity. As future work, in addition to the conditions set this time, it will examine whether there is a method that can generate a uniform constellation. It will continue to research whether Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) communication such as IEEE 802.11n can also be supported.

articleTitle: Real-Time Implementation of Modified LD-NET using Docker on NVIDIA Jetson Nano for Image Dehazing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Over the past few years, the majority of the industrial and surveillance sectors have observed visual sensor networks that record various images of the surrounding environment. The total surveillance systems are impacted by contaminated suspended air particles, which lowers the visual quality of the photos in stormy weather. Haze can interfere with motion analysis algorithms, leading to inaccurate tracking, trajectory prediction, or behaviour analysis of moving objects. The reduced visibility caused by hazing makes it difficult to capture and analyse the motion patterns and velocities of objects accurately. To tackle these challenges, we have used the Light-Dehaze Net (LD-Net) based on the Convolutional Neural Network algorithm in Deep Learning. Our suggested LD-Net uses a transformed atmospheric scattering model to jointly estimate the transmission map and the atmospheric light, in contrast to current learning-based methods that measure the transmission map and the atmospheric light separately. We implemented this LD-net model on NVIDIA Jetson Nano for real-time image dehazing application. Furthermore, we have added a Docker container to this implementation, where this container encapsulates the application and all its dependencies, including libraries, frameworks, and runtime environments. This portability allows the containerized application to run consistently across different environments.

articleTitle: Marine Debris Detection Model with Custom Dataset Using Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Object detection and instance segmentation are fundamental task in computer vision with applications ranging from autonomous driving to robotics. In this study, presented a custom dataset implementation on Mask R-CNN model, for object detection and instance segmentation. Our dataset images acquired from Motobu beach, Okinawa, Japan. Used to CV AT (Computer Vision Annotation Tool) for annotation. Containing a diverse range of objects of interest. Coastal debris affects marine ecosystem. The standard responses set in SGDs projects involve cutting down plastic waste at the source, beach cleanups, use of the circular economy, recycling, education, and a reduction in packaging, among other solutions. We fine-tuned the Mask R-CNN architecture using transfer learning techniques, initializing the model with weights pretrained on a large-scale dataset. Our proposed model is based on instance segmentation Mask R-CNN and SIFT (Scale invariant features transform) matching deep learning neural network. The results showed successfully recognize seven categories of marine debris, using a specific custom dataset. Marine debris global environmental issue and debris detection challenging, because of weather condition like (cloud, shine, and sunset), occulated and small size object, long distance from fix camera. Debris issues not only beaches but also under water and any localization. when the flood affects any area in the world, garbage is accumulated into deep sea. We developed a deep learning-based Mask R-CNN project for the marine environment auto-clean and multi-class classification process of marine debris detection from (Kakaxi fixed camera) images.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Framework for Human Recognition Using Gait Pattern Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Gait analysis has become a promising biometric method for identifying people, having special benefits including non-intrusiveness and potential long-range identification. The proposed methodology involves 2 different approaches: Temporal and Spatial. In the temporal approach, we use sequential machine learning models on the width, mass and width/mass vectors. In the spatial approach, we use convolutional neural networks on Gait Energy Image, Skeleton Gait Signature and Dynamic Image. To validate our method, we have used a standard gait dataset, CASIA-A. We achieve a best accuracy of 100% using the width vector on 0-degree view of CASIA-A. The results add to the literature in biometrics by offering insightful information and laying the groundwork for future developments in gait-based identification systems.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Various Histogram Equalization Techniques on Thermal Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper presents performance evaluation of various pre-processing techniques specifically on thermal images. Since thermal cameras often have lower resolution than RGB cameras, it might be difficult to successfully use their data for object recognition tasks. In the proposed work, the digital image processing-based techniques are applied on the thermal images to enhance the quality. The histogram equalization techniques along with their different variants, such as contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization, adaptive histogram equalization, plateau limit histogram equalization, brightness preserving bi-histogram equalization and minimum mean brightness error bi-histogram equalization (MMBEBHE) are utilized for the pre-processing. The performance is evaluated by computing the different parameters such as edge detection entropy score (EDES), peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) & blind reference less image spatial quality evaluator (BRISQUE), along with the computation time on various sets of images. It is observed that the MMBEBHE gives us better result with the lowest BRISQUE score and highest EDES score.

articleTitle: Accuracy assessment of a hand-held PPG based ECG acquisition device using 2-D CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper presents an accuracy assessment of a hand-held ECG acquisition device using 2-D convolutional neural network (CNN) based multi-classification of electrocardiogram (ECG) images. A deep learning-based classification model has been proposed in this paper to anticipate the user-friendly approach to ECG assessment. Many classification models have been proposed earlier for heart disease prediction, most of which have used spectrum analysis. However, in a practical scenario, a medical expert never prefers spectrum analysis or sampled ECG signals. In some critical cases, ECG is not fully conclusive, and other cardiac parameters are also required for accurate prediction of cardiac disease. Even though ECG image data is the key parameter to predict or detect heart disease for medical experts. Therefore, an image-based ECG classification approach has been proposed in this paper to provide an ease of access methodology for patients as well as for the medical expert. The proposed CNN-based classification model is trained and tested with the Kaggle ECG image dataset on the cloud, and the validation of the proposed model is performed on a real-time patients’ dataset taken from the Sanketlife ECG acquisition device. The testing accuracy for the proposed model is only 89.6%, as the ECG data acquired from the Sanketlife device is divided into several beats manually. The validation accuracy for the proposed algorithm is 97.29%.

articleTitle: AI-Based Model for Detection and Classification of Alzheimer Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Millions of people worldwide suffer from by the deadly brain disorder known as Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Alzheimer's disease is an incurable neurological disorder that affects brain function. To improve patient quality of life and create efficient treatment options, early AD diagnosis is essential. In this research, we have proposed a novel method for AD detection using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) datasets. We use a pre-trained CNN model to extract features from brain MRI images and classify them into Alzheimer's or non-Alzheimer's groups. We compare the efficiency of our model with several classifiers, such as: SoftMax, Support Vector Machine (SVM), DNN, and some other classifiers. We evaluated our model on an MRI dataset. We achieve high accuracy on the MRI dataset: 99.56% on the training set and 99% on the validation set. The loss values of training and validation are 0.0146% and 0.153% respectively. Our method is fast, robust, and generalizable. We point out that CNN-based models can be a powerful tool for AD detection using MRI data.

articleTitle: Scalability in Autoencoder-based OFDM Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: This paper proposed Scalability in Autoencoder-based Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing(OFDM) communication system. In the previous research, only the comparison between IEEE802.11a and Autoencoder by the conventional OFDM communication system was performed, and it was proved that the communication system created by Autoencoder exceeded the performance of the conventional system. Therefore, in this paper, it uses IEEE802.11n and compare whether it can be improved by expanding the bandwidth and using it.IEEE802.11n standard has an FFT length of 128, a subcarrier number of 114 (108 for data), and modulation schemes of Quadrature Phase Shift Keying(QPSK), 16 Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16QAM). The GI length is 800ns and the symbol length is 4000ns. In the simulation, a computer simulation was performed using a conventional OFDM communication system and a communication system generated by Autoencoder. Assuming that the simulation environment had an Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 0 to 30 and an amplitude r of 0.0 to 1.0, the Symbol Error Rate (SER) status for each SNR was output. As a result of computer simulation, QPSK converged at SNR 27 ㏈ at IEEE 802.11a, but was able to reduce SER overwhelmingly to SNR 12 ㏈ at IEEE 802.11n. Also, in 16QAM the convergence at r=0.0 is the same as for SNR22 ㏈, but in IEEE 802.11a it does not converge after r=0.6, but in IEEE 802.11n it does not converge only at r=0.9 and r=1.0 . As a future task, it will use IEEE802.11ac, which enables communication speeds several times faster than IEEE802.11n, examine whether it is possible to further improve accuracy. And it will continue our research to correspond MIMO communication.

articleTitle: Presentation Attack Detection for Sclera Biometric Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Reliability of a biometric system is judged by its ability to recognise genuine samples, reject impostors and the ability to withstand attacks in any form. A recognition sub-system does the job of accepting a genuine user and rejecting a non-user. The attack detection system tries to identify spoofs so that it can ensure that the sample obtained is from a live person. Proposed attack detection strategies can be used in ocular biometric recognition; more specifically, sclera recognition. Sclera recognition needs multi-angle eye images to capture larger portion of visible sclera. The process of obtaining multi-angle eye images is itself an active spoof detection strategy. It is performed by using a supervised eye-gaze detection deep learning model. In addition, passive spoof detection strategy detects fake images by examining the nature of image captured. Such images are classified by using a DenseNet based supervised deep learning model. Individually both these subsystems achieves about 99 % accuracy. Collective implementation of both these systems gives about 100% accuracy. The proposed attack detection strategy can be implemented in a smart phone with ocular biometrics.

articleTitle: Sclera Vessel Analysis for Biometric System on Real Time Security Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Biometrics has an unavoidable space in the era of security in terms of identifying the Individuals. There are many biometrics which are providing more prominent result, but all these biometrics needs the user cooperation in acquisition. The sclera, white portion of the eye, vessel patterns are holding the uniqueness to identify the individuals. This becomes the root of many researchers to recognize the individual with non-co-operative user images. Sclera recognitions are beginning of the new era which is to leads the recognition on the surveillance camera. Since the Image quality is less in the surveillance camera images and the segmentation of sclera is more challenging which has more impact on the accuracy of the recognition. To improve the accuracy of the segmentation Convolutional Neural Network has been used which has increase the time complexity of the system. Since the accuracy of the segmentation has increased and to optimize the time integro Differential Operator is utilized which reduces the searching area of the iris so the time taken will be reduced. The combination of CNN and DIO will increase the accuracy and complexity of the Segmentation Process. The experiments are carried out on the UBIRIS Dataset V2.

articleTitle: The Art of Deception: Novel Graphical User Authentication Scheme Using Illusion Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: User authentication is a crucial component of information security and can be accomplished through various ways. Strong text-based password authentication techniques have been used for ages, and they are normally expected to provide some level of security. But users may be forced to write down their passwords on paper or even store them in a computer file because it can be difficult to commit such strong passwords to memory. The use of graphical authentication in place of text-based authentication has been suggested as a way to combat such tendencies. This has been prompted by the fact that people naturally tend to remember visuals over words more readily. In this research, we present a novel challenge-response authentication scheme based on three types of illusions. i.e., Literal Illusion, Cognitive Illusion and Physiological Illusion. And 4 sub-categories of Cognitive Illusion i.e. Cognitive Distorting Illusion, Cognitive Paradox Illusion, Cognitive Ambiguous Illusion and Cognitive Fictional Illusion. To find out how satisfied users are with the suggested scheme's performance and usability, an experimental research and survey have been done. The study's findings demonstrate that the proposed system is secure, user- friendly, and can withstand typical password attacks such as brute - force attempts and shoulder surfing.

articleTitle: Enhancing Patient Care and Monitoring Through AI and IoT in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: AI and IoT can revolutionize patient care and monitoring. This presentation discusses the pros and cons of using AI and IoT to enhance patient care, therapy, and remote patient monitoring. AI technology improve data analysis, predictive modeling, and decision-making while IoT devices simplify patient data collecting and transfer. These technologies may enhance treatment regimens, patient results, and insights. AI and IoT let healthcare practitioners remotely monitor patients. Wearable sensors, remote monitoring devices, and implantable devices may collect vital signs, activity levels, and other health data from patients. Then, real-time artificial intelligence systems may analyze the data for quicker diagnosis, better treatment, and better results. AI-enhanced predictive analytics may help doctors identify patterns and trends in patient data for early diagnosis, risk assessment, and prevention. Machine learning algorithms can predict disease development, adjust medication dosages, and identify potential adverse events to enhance patient safety and treatment efficacy. However, healthcare AI and IoT use raises concerns that must be addressed. The massive volumes of patient data collected and transferred pose data security and privacy concerns. The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and patient privacy must be observed. Data integration, standardization, and compatibility are some of the technical challenges of IoT device and AI system integration. Healthcare firms need robust infrastructure and data management to network, share data, and collaborate across devices and systems. Finally, AI and IoT technologies may enhance patient care and monitoring in the healthcare business. AI algorithms fordata analysis and IoT devices for real-time data collection may help doctors diagnose, treat, and monitor patients remotely. Data security, privacy, and interoperability must be addressed to deploy AI and IoT in health care. AI and IoT might transform healthcare and enhance patient outcomes despite these challenges.

Author Keywords: AI and IoT a Digital Environment

articleTitle: MLSD-GAN - Generating Strong High Quality Face Morphing Attacks Using Latent Semantic Disentanglement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Face-morphing attacks are a growing concern for biometric researchers, as they can be used to fool face recognition systems (FRS). These attacks can be generated at the image level (supervised) or representation level (unsupervised). Previous unsupervised morphing attacks have relied on generative adver-sarial networks (GANs). More recently, researchers have used linear interpolation of StyleGAN-encoded images to generate morphing attacks. In this paper, we propose a new method for generating high-quality morphing attacks using StyleGAN disentanglement. Our approach, called MLSD-GAN, spherically interpolates the disentangled latents to produce realistic and diverse morphing attacks. We evaluate the vulnerability of MLSD-GAN on two deep-learning-based FRS techniques. The results show that MLSD-GAN poses a significant threat to FRS, as it can generate morphing attacks that are highly effective at fooling these systems.

articleTitle: Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) Based Robust Watermarking Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Digital watermarking is a widely used technique for embedding information into digital media to protect intellectual property rights. However, digital watermarks are vulnerable to various types of malicious attacks. In this paper, we propose an AES-based watermarking scheme to further improve the security and robustness of an existing watermark technique. The proposed scheme involves embedding the original watermark into the host image using a watermarking technique, and then encrypting the embedded watermark using the AES algorithm. The watermarked image is then subjected to a series of attacks and then is decrypted using the same AES algorithm. To assess the performance of the proposed approach in terms of security and robustness, it is implemented and tested on a set of images. The experimental findings demonstrate that, while maintaining a low distortion rate, the proposed technique offers high robustness against various attacks. The proposed AES-based watermarking scheme can be considered as an effective and secure solution for protecting digital watermarks in various applications.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Traffic signs play a crucial role in conveying important information to drivers on the road, including speed limits, turn regulations, and other rules. Traffic Sign Detection technology has been developed to assist drivers in complying with traffic rules, enabling early warning to avoid rule violations. However, existing traffic sign detection systems have limitations such as incorrect predictions and high hardware and maintenance costs. The proposed system uses a deep learning algorithm to identify and classify traffic signs, with a web camera feature that detects and displays screens for closer viewing. This helps drivers save valuable moments by reducing the probability of rule-breaking-related accidents. Advanced technologies like convolutional neural networks (CNN) can enhance the performance of traffic sign detection systems, providing accurate and reliable information in real time. This paper presents new innovations in PC vision and transportation engineering by using the German Traffic Sign Recognition (GTSRB) dataset to represent different types of traffic signals in the world's space. The paper presents a unique CNN architecture designed specifically for traffic signal models, showing a deep understanding of the specific capabilities and problems associated with traffic signals, potentially leading to the accuracy of the first class. The findings may also reveal a noticeable improvement in overall performance metrics, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed method

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach Of Differential Evolution And Multistage LSTM For Diagnosis Of Psychiatric Disorder Using EEG
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Individuals' mental health and quality of life are significantly impacted by psychiatric illnesses. This research describes a unique method for reliably identifying mental diseases based on electroencephalogram (EEG) data. Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) is used for feature selection with reduction, while Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) is used for classification. PSO is used to extract the most informative features from high-dimensional EEG data, whilst LSTM is utilised to capture temporal relationships within the signals. The research looks at five types of mental disorders: ‘Addictive disorder,’ ‘Trauma and stress-related disorder, ‘Obsessive-compulsive disorder,’ ‘Schizophrenia,’ and ‘Anxiety disorder’. To begin, PSO is used to optimise a fitness function and find the most significant characteristics, lowering the complexity of the EEG dataset. This stage removes unnecessary and superfluous characteristics, resulting in improved classification performance. Following that, the reduced feature set is put into an LSTM-based classifier, which learns patterns and correlations in the EEG signals. The model is trained on labelled data and its performance is assessed with a validation set. The suggested method obtains a validation accuracy of 90 %, proving its efficacy in effectively detecting and discriminating between various mental diseases.

articleTitle: Glaucoma Classification Using Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Glaucoma is a severe eye disease that damages the optic nerve over time, often due to high intraocular pressure from accumulated aqueous humor. This pressure results from drainage system blockage connecting the iris and cornea. Consequently, optic nerve damage impairs visual signal transmission to the brain, causing vision loss and potential blindness, typically affecting those in their fifties and older. Unfortunately, a cure is elusive unless detected and treated early. Early glaucoma diagnosis is challenging, but regular screenings are vital. However, this process is often costly, tedious, and prone to human error, influenced by screening methods, resource availability, skilled ophthalmologists, equipment, and more. This paper introduces an innovative glaucoma detection method by automating and combining classical techniques. Upon receiving an image, it undergoes processing to segment the optic cup and optic disc using our CNN architecture. Output is then processed to fit ellipses to the contours, assessing the major axis ratio for diagnosis. In a second approach, a SeResnet152 architecture is trained to distinguish Glaucoma from N on-Glaucoma fundus images. The model achieves segmentation dice scores of 0.79 and 0.91 on a validation set of 183 retinal fundus images and an AUC score of 0.936 for classifying glaucoma-positive images.

articleTitle: Elevating Fingerprint Matching with a Unified dHash, SIFT, and LSH Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: User authentication is essential for maintaining the security, privacy, and integrity of systems and data. It ensures that only authorized individuals can access specific resources, applications, or sensitive information, preventing potential data breaches, unauthorized modifications, or malicious activities. Biometric identification, particularly fingerprint recognition, has revolutionized authentication. This research paper proposes combining cutting-edge algorithms such as dHash, SIFT-Harris feature points, and Locality-Sensitive hashes to create a more efficient fingerprint-matching system. It aims to improve matching accuracy, data breach avoidance, robustness, and processing speed in fingerprint recognition systems. The final proposed model works for almost all altered (obliteration, central rotation, and z-cut) images. A total of 55,273 images were tested, giving an accuracy of 0.99.

articleTitle: GeometricSMOTE-Enhanced Deep Gaussian Mixture Models for Imbalanced Data Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Imbalanced data classification poses a challenge in machine learning due to limited minority class samples, impacting model performance. We propose an innovative solution merging Geometric Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and Deep Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) for improved classification. Geometric SMOTE generates synthetic samples by considering geometric relationships with nearest neighbors, enhancing Deep GMM training. Deep GMM captures complex data distributions and generates realistic samples, bridging minority-majority class gaps. Integrating Geometric SMOTE synthetic samples enables Deep GMM to learn representative data patterns, improving classification performance. Experiments on benchmarks exhibit the approach's effectiveness. GeometricSMOTE-enhanced Deep GMM notably enhances accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score for the minority class. The approach remains robust across imbalanced ratios and dataset traits, a promising solution for real-world imbalanced data challenges. It enhances deep learning models' performance, offering valuable utility.

articleTitle: A Review on Anti-Spoofing : Face Manipulation and Liveness Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The latest developments in deep generative networks have greatly improved the quality of generating life-like fake face videos. Face digital manipulation such as DeepFakes, FaceSwap, and Face2Face are critical issues for automated face recognition systems as it detrimentally affects their performance. To tackle this difficulty, face anti-spoofing is utilized which is a task to prevent unauthorized entry by breaching facial recognition systems using a mask, photo, video or another substitute for a legitimate person's face. The review paper examines the problems and solutions explored in the domain of digital face manipulation, as well as the notion of liveliness detection and numerous aspects and cues that can be used to determine the authenticity of a face. The review is organized into sections, discussing face manipulation techniques, liveness detection using eye blinking, and finally a hybrid system is proposed that considers both face manipulation and liveness detection to strengthen existing solutions. It aims to enhance the security and reliability of facial recognition technology in various applications.

articleTitle: Lung Disease Classification in Chest X-Rays with Feature Fusion via Stacked Convolutional Denoising Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Deep Learning recently has made a breakthrough and tremendous advancement in medical imaging domain. While training supervised deep learning models require large number of annotated data. This is costlier, challenging and time-consuming and requires domain expertise. Nevertheless, these challenges can be tackled with models trained in unsupervised manner., that requires no annotations. Stacked convolutional denoising autoencoders are unsupervised models with convolutional layers that reconstruct the original input data that requires no annotated data with random perturbations added to the original input data. The ability to combine information from various sources in enhancing classification performance is showing promising results. In this paper, we show unsupervised models with stacked convolutional denoising autoencoders for extracting salient features from input un annotated data and fine tuning it for supervised classification of lung diseases on chest X-ray images with feature fusion.

articleTitle: Estimation of Student's Interest Reaction Levels in Class Video
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Estimation of Student's Interest Reaction Levels using class video analysis will help the researcher to understand a level of human pose estimation. AI model estimate the Interest reaction levels that can capture and quantify with high accuracy, the degree of reaction when a student is performing various tasks. The model achieves by detecting changes in muscle movements that reveal differences in facial expression that occur when a student is interested in the class or not. In this research, we have designed and implemented a system that detect student reaction and behavior based on keypoint detection. Here, this paper propose a method to detect a person from the video using OpenPose, and extract the coordinate data of the joints. This method improve the detection accuracy of the face direction, facial attitude and degree of reaction by calculating coordinate data of each person with facial expression. The proposed method aims to enhance interest reaction results by not only assessing where a person is looking but also by analyzing facial expressions.

articleTitle: Driver's Facial Expression Recognition Using Global Context Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Driver's facial expression recognition plays a critical role in enhancing driver safety, comfort, and overall driving experience by proactively mitigating potential road risks. While most existing works in this domain rely on CNN - based approaches, this paper proposes a novel method for driver facial expression recognition using Global Context Vision Transformer (DFER-GCViT). With its inherent capabilities of transformer-based architectures and global context modeling, the proposed method handles challenges commonly encountered in real-world driving scenarios, including occlusions, head pose variations, and illumination conditions. Our method consists of three modules: preprocessing for face detection and data augmentation, facial feature extraction of local and global features, and expression classification using a modified GC-ViT classifier. To evaluate the performance of DFER-GCViT, extensive experiments are conducted on two benchmarking datasets namely the KMU-FED driver facial expression dataset and FER2013 general facial expression dataset. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of DFER-GCViT in accurately recognizing driver's facial expressions, achieving an average accuracy of 98.27 % on the KMU-FED dataset and 73.78% on the FER2013 dataset, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods on these two benchmarking datasets.

articleTitle: Rice Impact Illness Acknowledgment Employing a Profound Convolutional Neural Arrange
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Rice illness acknowledgment is vital in robotized rice illness conclusion frameworks. At display, profound convolutional neural arrange (CNN) is for most often regarded as the cutting-edge setup for image recognition. In this research, we suggest a brand-new CNN-based rice impact acknowledgment technique. For the reason of creating and checking the CNN show, the database consists of 2902 negative tests and 2906 positive tests. In addition, as part of our assessment We conduct testing for both qualitative and quantitative comparisons of the suggested plan's appropriateness. The results of the investigation suggest that high-level highlights mined from CNN are more accurate and beneficial than previously hand-crafted highlights such closest double designs histograms (LBPH) and Haar-WT (Wavelet Change). Additionally, the numerical evaluation's findings show that, compared to both LBPH and Softmax using CNN, Support Vector Machine (SVM) with CNN performs similarly, with higher precision, a larger area beneath curves (AUC), and better recipient working properties (ROC) curves. and Haar-WT, which both also use SVMs as the classifier. This might perhaps make our CNN programs the greatest method for detecting rice impact illness and might be applied in practical situations.

articleTitle: Does ChatGPT Spell the End of Automatic Question Generation Research?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: We explore the potential of utilizing ChatGPT to automatically generate educational assessment questions. Despite the growing promise of ChatGPT across various natural language tasks, including question generation, there exists a challenge of producing content that is both reliable and desirable. This issue becomes particularly crucial in educational assessments, where the quality of the generated content and its alignment with the assessed material are paramount. This research examines questions produced by ChatGPT, focusing on their alignment with different levels of Bloom's Taxonomy and their overall fluency and coherence. To assess the quality of the generated questions, we establish several scenarios for generation and subsequently evaluate the questions using both automated metrics and manual examination. Our empirical analysis shows that ChatGPT tends to produce high-quality questions; however, these questions predominantly fall within the categories of Remember, Understand, and Apply in Bloom's Taxonomy. It exhibits limited capacity for generating questions that require higher-order reasoning. Further enhancements are therefore necessary to enhance the question quality of this model, particularly with regard to the diversity of question types based on Bloom's Taxonomy. This improvement is crucial to ensure the suitability of the generated questions for effective classroom assessments.

articleTitle: Image Captioning with Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Image captioning involves generating a natural language description that accurately represents the content and context of an image. To achieve this, image captioning utilises various machine learning techniques and fields, such as computer vision and natural language processing. In the field of image captioning, a lot of advances have been made with encoder-decoder models and reinforcement learning algorithms. However, there are still problems of imbalance between testing and training, as reinforcement learning only handles single comparator metrics such as CIDEr, SPICE, and BLEU and could not perform better in multiple metrics at once. Which is why a lack of diversity can be seen in generated captions. This idea proposes a general technique for collaborative updating that can bridge the gap between evaluation measures and test metrics to produce captions that are more human-like. To increase the precision of image captions, the approach involves using a compiled reward system that considers multiple evaluation metrics to compare the generated sentence with the provided sentences. We will evaluate the model's performance and the reward updating process on standard datasets like MS COCO.

articleTitle: Efficient Medical Supply Chain Forecasting Using Time Series Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The unexpected shortage of potentially life-saving medication can result in the loss of lives, while overstocking can strain financial resources and generate medical waste. Due to this reason, forecasting techniques are of great concern to address this medical inventory management challenge. The paper presents an AI-based strategy for foreseeing medical store inventories using time-series analysis. The approach aims at predicting inventory variations and delivers order demand forecasts by incorporating temporal patterns and trends in historical data. Time series learning models are a subset of algorithms specifically developed to analyze and extract important insights from sequential data, where the order and timing of the data points are crucial. A comprehensive approach, namely the augmented dickey-fuller (ADF) test, is employed as a pre-processing technique to assess stationarity data and ensure statistical properties like mean and variance remain consistent over time. This work utilizes advanced time series forecasting methods and machine learning algorithms to model inventory fluctuations, capturing long-term dependencies and nonlinear patterns in the data. Out of all the applied techniques, seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA) outperformed autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) as well as extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). SARIMA showed minimum root mean square error which is 265.7 for order demand forecasting.

articleTitle: Improving Stock Market Forecasting Using Advanced Time Series Analysis Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The mechanism of a stock exchange is very dynamic and intricate, making it difficult to forecast its conduct. A typical method for analyzing historical stock market data and predicting future trends is time series data analysis. With this strategy, past stock market data is examined for patterns, trends, and correlations to spot prospective market shifts in the future. Moving averages, autoregressive models, and exponential smoothing are a few statistical methods used in Improving Stock Market Forecasting using Advanced Time Series Analysis Techniques to find periodic and unusual changes in data. These techniques may be used to provide projections based on past data, empowering traders, and investors to choose when and how to purchase and sell stocks with more knowledge. Because of the erratic and unpredictable nature of the market, forecasting the stock market remains a difficult subject despite advances in time series analytic tools. This research intends to improve the precision of the Holt-Winters model and Simple moving average by using so-phisticated forecasting methods and optimisation algorithms via a thorough investigation of Improving Stock Market Forecasting using Advanced Time Series Analysis prediction which gives a more efficient result

articleTitle: A Study on Effective Segmentation Network in MRI Images for Diagnosis of Brain Tumor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: Brain glioma type's tumors are among the most toxic cancers worldwide. Now-a-days, due to the advance of convolutional neural networks, many brain tumor segmentation systems aid clinicians to diagnose and operate. To support clinicians in the accurate automatic semantic segmentation of brain tumors, we investigate two convolutional encoding-decoding neural network i.e. UNet and PSPNet for brain glioma tumour segmentation from multimodal MRI images. The study is trained from the 2020 Brain Tumour Segmentation (BraTS) challenge. A rigorous assessment and comparative evaluation on the BraTS'20 validation set and test set, respectively, evolved with the PSPN et architecture achieving dice scores of 0.876 and 0.905 for enhancing tumour region and necrotic tumour/core region, respectively and with the UN et architecture achieving dice scores of 0.842 and 0.908 for enhancing tumour region and necrotic tumour/core region, respectively.

articleTitle: Empowering Smart Cities: A Comprehensive Edge Computing Framework for Enhanced IoT Situation Awareness
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) / Web of Things (WoT) presents numerous advantages for the development of intelligent cities. With the help of a vast array of diverse IoT devices, these cities can collect a tremendous amount of data, opening up opportunities for advanced analysis and insights. Given the diversity of information sources in smart cities, processing these data and extracting meaningful insights for decision-makers is a significant hurdle. While the conventional cloud computing paradigm offers substantial computing and storage capabilities for this purpose, it necessitates transferring all data from user endpoint edge equipment to the cloud, thereby causing considerable latency. Our study aims to mitigate the latency issue in data processing by utilizing the edge computing technique. Since a significant amount of data originates from user endpoint devices, handling the data at the edge can enhance overall performance. Our findings reveal that conducting raw IoT data processing at the edge devices yields a seamless situational awareness for smart city decision-makers while minimizing latency.

articleTitle: IoT Empowered AI: Transforming Object Recognition and NLP Summarization with Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision and Machine Intelligence (CVMI)
abstract: In anticipation of the widespread adoption of augmented reality in the future, this paper introduces an advanced mobile application that seamlessly integrates AR and IoT technologies. The application aims to make these cutting-edge technologies more affordable and accessible to users while highlighting their immense benefits in assisting with household appliance control, as well as providing interactive and educational experiences.
